memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Abraham had taken another wife, whose name was Keturah. She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah. Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan; the descendants of Dedan were the Ashurites, the Letushites and the Leummites. The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanok, Abida and Eldaah. All these were descendants of Keturah." - Gen 25:1-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a long list of names — some we can barely pronounce, most we will never hear of again. Yet the Bible pauses to record them. Abraham, now well past a hundred, still had a fruitful life through Keturah, and God let his family branch out into many peoples.

For us, these names quietly say something about God. He notices people. Nobody here is a "big name," yet each one is written down. God is not only the God of famous heroes; He is the God who knows and remembers ordinary lives (Luke 12:6-7). Your name may never appear in a history book, but it is known to your Maker.

We also see God's faithfulness spreading. Long ago God promised Abraham that he would be the father of many nations (Gen 17:4-5), and even these sons of Keturah are part of that promise unfolding. God keeps His word, sometimes in ways we only notice by reading a list of names.

If you ever feel small, unnoticed, or overlooked, remember: the God who wrote down Ishbak and Shuah knows you by name. You matter to Him, and He is still writing His faithful story through ordinary families like yours.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God knows and values me even when I feel unnoticed?
2. How have I seen God's faithfulness unfold quietly over time?
3. Am I faithful in the "ordinary" parts of life that no one applauds?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You know each of us by name, even the ones the world forgets. Help me to trust that my ordinary life matters to You. Amen.
